name: LMS — Bilingual Learning Management System
oneLiner: A bilingual (English/Khmer) learning management system for course delivery, assessment, communication, and academic analytics.
question: Can one bilingual workspace make course delivery, assessment, and student support calm enough for schools and training teams in Cambodia?
problem: Teaching operations are scattered across chat apps, spreadsheets, and paper: course plans in one place, assignments in another, grades in a third, and student communication everywhere. For bilingual institutions, most off-the-shelf tools also assume English-only users.
targetUsers: Schools, universities, and training teams — with distinct role experiences for teachers, students, and administrators, in English and Khmer.
whyItMatters: Academic operations software shapes how teachers spend their time. A workspace designed for the bilingual reality of Cambodian institutions lowers the barrier for schools that current LMS products treat as an afterthought.
exactRole: [OWNER_INPUT_REQUIRED: Your exact role — solo build or team, and which parts are yours]
teamContributions: [OWNER_INPUT_REQUIRED: Teammates and their parts, or 'Independent project']
research: [OWNER_INPUT_REQUIRED: What you studied before building — existing LMS products, teacher interviews, school workflows?]
validation: The product is deployed as a public walkthrough prototype and labels itself as such on its own interface. No school or training team is using it in real operations yet, and this page does not claim otherwise.
proposedSolution: One accessible workspace covering the teaching lifecycle: plan courses, deliver lessons, assess work, message students, and track progress through academic analytics — with role-based views (teacher, student, admin) and full English/Khmer experiences.
userWorkflow: A teacher plans a course and publishes lessons
Students receive assignments and submit work
Assessment and grades flow into per-class progress views
Messages keep student communication inside the workspace
Academic analytics summarize progress across every class
systemArchitecture: Next.js application deployed on Vercel; the public walkthrough demonstrates the full interface with sample data. [OWNER_INPUT_REQUIRED: Backend, database, and auth details once you want them public]
methods: Role-based interface design (teacher, student, administrator), bilingual UX as a first-class requirement rather than a translation pass, and accessibility by default — responsive, keyboard-friendly, mobile-ready.
businessValue: The prototype includes product framing beyond the software itself — features, solutions, lifecycle, and pricing pages — treating the LMS as a commercial product exploration, not just an interface exercise. Commercial viability remains untested until real institutions pilot it.
contractsPolicy: A real deployment would sit on institutional contracts: service agreements with schools, acceptable-use terms for students, and clear data-processing commitments. Drafting those is part of taking this beyond a prototype.
dataPrivacy: Student records are sensitive data. The public walkthrough runs on sample data only; a real pilot would need data-minimization, retention rules, and guardian-appropriate consent before any real student information enters the system.
risks: A polished walkthrough can be mistaken for a production system — the interface labels itself a prototype to prevent exactly that
Student-data privacy failures would harm minors — which is why real data stays out until governance is designed
Grading and progress displays must be verifiably correct before any institution relies on them
humanApprovalPoints: Any pilot with a real school — and any real student data — requires a designed consent and privacy review first
Grades and academic records remain teacher-owned decisions; the system records, it does not decide
Pricing and contractual commitments require human sign-off
technicalDecisions: Next.js with a component-driven interface for the role-based views
Bilingual English/Khmer experiences designed in from the start, not retrofitted
Public walkthrough deployment with sample data, labeled as a prototype on the interface itself
Accessible by default: responsive, keyboard-friendly, mobile-ready

completedWork.text: Public walkthrough covering the product surface: dashboard, courses, calendar, assignments, messages, grades, analytics, and settings across teacher/student/admin roles
Product framing pages: features, solutions, lifecycle, pricing, and resources
Pilot with a real school or training team

evidence.text: The walkthrough prototype is publicly deployed and clickable — anyone can explore the full interface.
The interface labels itself a walkthrough prototype and runs on sample data — the claim discipline is built into the product page itself.

results.text: A complete, deployed product walkthrough exists; no institutional usage, performance, or commercial results are claimed yet.

constraints: No real institution has piloted it, so every workflow assumption is unvalidated against actual school operations
The privacy and consent design a real pilot needs does not exist yet
tradeoffs: Building the full product surface first (including pricing) trades early validation for a complete demonstration HR and pilot partners can actually click through
Sample data keeps the walkthrough safe but means no claim about real-data behavior can be made
